questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

The introduction of

A. ­had ruled from the time man learned to cook food

B­. meant the end of firewood, which

C­. the kerosene stove also
questions.solution: The first sentence in the sequence should tell us ''the introduction of what?'' This is only given in sentence C. So it is the first sentence. It should be followed by B and A respectively. No other sequence can be logical or grammatically correct. So option 3 is correct.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

Tina said to him, “Please wait here till I return.”

options.text: Tina asked him to stay there.
Tina requested him to wait there till she returned.
Tina request him to wait until she comes.
Tina says he should wait there till her returned.

questions.solution:
The correct is __option 2)__ i.e.* Tina requested him to wait there till she returned*.

__Explanation__:

__
 
• We make changes in tenses of reported speech only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• When the reported speech is an **Imperative**** **sentence, we follow these steps-
 
 
• Reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'requested';** **as **'please' **is given in 'Reported Speech'
 
• connector 'that' is used in place of commas.
 
• Tense of reported speech will be changed from **Present **to **past Tense** (in above sentence- 'return' changes into 'returned')
 
• personal Pronouns of reported speech are changed as per subject and object of reporting verb. Here, the first person- 'I' will change into 'She' as per **Subject** - 'Tina'.
 
 

Indirect speech__:

__
 
• By following these steps we get the final sentence: ​*" Tina requested him to wait there till she returned*.*."​*

Mistake Point__:

 
• We may think that 'wait' is a **Verb **here, so it should be changed into 'waited'
 
• Always do remember if the **'Reporting verb' **is in 'Past Tense' the 'Tense' of 'Indirect speech' will be changed.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

The girl caught the kite.

options.text: The kite was caught by the girl.
The kite is caught by the girl
The kite was catch by the girl.
The kite is catch by the girl.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The kite was caught by the girl.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the **active** voice and 'The girl' is the subject and '**the kite**' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into **passive** voice, the subject 'The girl' becomes the object, the object 'the kite' becomes the subject.
 
• The active format "V2 (caught)" should be converted into the passive format "was + V3 "
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

______ worst is yet to come.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ** 'The'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The worst is the **Superlative degree**.
 
• There is nothing more than a Superlative degree. So we must use the definite article ''**the**'' before worst.
 
• Hence, A and An are not the correct answer. 
 
• **Thus, the complete sentence is: ***The worst is yet to come.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• We do not need to add the definite article if the noun is possessive: 

 **Example: **

 
 
• **That’s** his **best**
 
• **He’s **my **most diligent**
 
 
 
• **​**The is not used with superlatives in predicative position, when we compare the same person or thing in different situations.

 **Example: **He is nicest in the evenings after he has had a few drinks. (NOT He is the nicest in the evenings …)

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Every effect we see, hear or speak in our outside (1)/ or physical world has a specific cause that (2)/ have its origin in the inner or mental world. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__3__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• If a **subject **and the **verb **are **joined by a relative pronoun, **the **verb **used will **agree with the antecedent **to the relative pronoun.

 **Example: **She is one of the noblest **women** that **has** ever lived on the earth. (wrong)

 She is one of the noblest **women **that **have **ever lived on the earth. (right) 
 
• **Cause** is **singular** therefore the verb must also be singular. Therefore we must use '**has**' instead of 'have.' So option 3 is the correct answer. 

**Thus, the correct answer is: ***Every effect we see, hear or speak in our outside or physical world has **a specific cause** that **has** its origin in the inner or mental world.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Photosynthesis is (1)/possible (2)/because of sun. (3)/No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__3__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **'the sun' **should be there in place of **'sun'**
 
• **The definite article (the)** is used **in front of nouns that are only one in nature like sun, moon, earth, etc.**
 
• **Example: **

 the North pole, the South pole, the earth, the world, the universe, the sun, the moon, the sky, the air, the weather, the wind, the rain, the sea, the planet
 
• **Thus, the correct sentence is:* ****Photosynthesis is possible because of** the sun.***
